pr.title: feat(etag): allow for custom hashing methods to be used to etag

summary: This PR adds support for custom hashing algorithms to the etag middleware by accepting an optional `generateDigest` function parameter. The change allows users to override the default SHA-1 algorithm with alternatives like SHA-256. The main risk is that the signature of the internal `generateDigest` function changed, requiring all callers to be updated.

findings.rationale: The internal `generateDigest` function signature changed from `(stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null)` to `(stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null, generator: (body: Uint8Array) => ArrayBuffer | Promise<ArrayBuffer>)`. While this is an internal function, if any external code or tests directly import and call `generateDigest` from `digest.ts`, they will break. The diff shows the call site was updated, but there's a risk of missed callers.
findings.suggestedCheck: Search the codebase and any dependent packages for direct imports of `generateDigest` from `src/middleware/etag/digest.ts` to ensure no external callers are broken.

findings.rationale: The line `await c.res.blob() // Force using body` was removed from the 304 Not Modified response path. This line may have been important for ensuring the response body was fully consumed before sending a 304. Removing it could potentially leave the body unconsumed in some edge cases, though 304 responses should have no body by spec.
findings.suggestedCheck: Verify that removing `await c.res.blob()` does not cause issues with response body handling or resource cleanup in the 304 Not Modified case. Check if this line was necessary for any cleanup or side effects.

findings.rationale: The new test only verifies that a custom SHA-256 algorithm produces the expected etag values. It does not test error handling if the custom `generateDigest` function throws an error or returns an invalid value. Edge cases like null/undefined returns or rejected promises are not covered.
findings.suggestedCheck: Consider adding tests for error scenarios: what happens if `generateDigest` throws, rejects, or returns an unexpected type? Verify the middleware handles these gracefully.
